tooltip: Rule of Thirds Grid - Divides the frame into 9 equal parts
content1: Divides the frame into 9 equal parts using 2 vertical and 2 horizontal lines. One of the most widely used composition techniques in photography and videography.
content2: Place your subject along one of the 4 lines or at one of the 4 intersection points (called power points) for a naturally balanced and visually engaging composition.
content3: Landscape photography, portrait framing, horizon placement, and any scene where the subject is off-center.
content4: Avoid placing the horizon in the center of the frame. Instead align it with the top or bottom third line depending on whether the sky or foreground is more interesting.

tooltip: Center Grid - Symmetric composition guide with diagonals
content1: Draws a centered cross and diagonal lines across the frame. Ideal for symmetric and geometrically centered compositions.
content2: Align your subject exactly at the center intersection for a strong symmetric look. The diagonal lines help identify leading lines and geometric balance.
content3: Architecture, symmetrical subjects, tunnel shots, reflections, and formal portraits.
content4: Center composition works best when the subject itself is symmetric. Pair it with strong leading lines converging toward the center for maximum impact.

tooltip: Golden Ratio Grid - Based on the mathematical ratio 1.618
content1: Based on the mathematical golden ratio (φ ≈ 1.618), considered the most aesthetically pleasing proportion found in nature, art, and architecture.
content2: Place your primary subject at one of the 4 intersection points of the golden ratio lines. The spiral arcs in each quadrant indicate the natural flow the human eye follows.
content3: Fine art photography, portraits, nature scenes, and any composition where a more organic and refined balance is desired over the rule of thirds.
content4: Position the most important element of your scene where the spiral tightens — this is the natural focal point your viewer's eye will be drawn to first.

tooltip: Square Grid - Uniform grid overlay for precise alignment
content1: Overlays a uniform square grid across the entire frame. Each cell is sized at 1/6th of the smaller frame dimension, providing a consistent spatial reference.
content2: Use the grid lines as alignment guides to keep horizontal and vertical elements straight and evenly spaced across the frame.
content3: Architectural photography, product shots, flat lays, and any scene requiring precise geometric alignment or symmetry.
content4: Enable this grid when shooting flat lay compositions or architecture to ensure no unintentional tilt or misalignment in your frame.
